thread:
Aisha: hey @sam @kai — need a concise set of bench runs for the launch post + webinar. ask: p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/s, and end-to-end time for 1k/2k/8k seq. also need cold vs warmed cache numbers and the payloads used. deadline: EOD Thu (72h). keep it minimal please :pray:

Sam: got it. can you confirm model variant (gpt-rlhf-1 / gpt-open-quant)? also do you want quantized runs (int8) vs fp16 baseline? and traffic mix (50% chat completions, 50% single-turn gen?)

Ben: for webinar we'll want a small "real traffic" prompt set (10–20 prompts) and a synthetic mix (100 prompts). also request GPU mem / utilization if possible. p99 is most important for customer narrative.

Kai: note: prefix/KV caching will change numbers a lot. we'll do three controlled runs: cold (no cache), warmed (same session reuse), and prefix-cached (common prefixes). we'll also log kernel selection and batch sizes. give us your golden prompt files and target seq lengths.

Aisha: golden set: I'll drop two files in the marketing folder — `launch_golden_prompts.txt` (15 prompts) and `webinar_synthetic.jsonl` (100). include short context/metadata lines. also prioritize p95+p99 in the post. thanks.

Sam: plan: 1) smoke run today on a small sample 2) full runs tomorrow — int8 and fp16, sequences 1k/2k/8k, cold/warm/prefix. collector will produce CSV per run with columns: run_id, model, quant, seq_len, cache_state, p50_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, tokens_per_s, gpu_mem_mb, notes

Kai: example command (will run under `/bench/runtime/launch`):
```
./run_bench --model gpt-rlhf-1 --quant int8 --seq 2048 --prompts marketing/launch_golden_prompts.txt --cache_state warmed --reps 200
```

deploy-bot: scheduled bench job 1769010001 by Sam (eng-runtime) — status: queued :gear:

Ben: please include raw logs + a short README explaining load profile and any anomalies.

Aisha: deadline still EOD Thu — can we get at least the smoke run CSV by EOD tomorrow? will prep marketing narrative once we have p95 numbers.

Sam: yes — smoke CSV by tomorrow EOD. full CSVs after second run. we will annotate known caveats (kernel fallbacks, transient OOMs).

Kai: tagging @ops for any infra throttles during high-seq runs.

Aisha: perfect. appreciate the quick turn. :rocket:
